# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 16
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 16

---

*[THE BRIGHTNESS. THE COMMISSION. Peter wants to stay.]*

1. We — all twelve of us — watched him as though he were being lifted into the heavens. The brightness in him never stopped. It kept radiating, ceaselessly.

2. And all around him, all the righteous — I saw them — blazing with a brightness ten times the sun. Their whiteness was beyond any snow.

3. The joy in paradise was immense. They praised God, they and all the angels together, voices filling everything.

4. The Lord turned to us. "Do you see the glory here?" he said. "Do you see those who are with me? What do you think this vision means? What will become of it?"

5. We looked at each other. "We don't understand," we said. "Before we could even form a thought, our understanding was taken away."

6. The Lord said to me: "Go. Tell everyone who is to enter my kingdom — in the way of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. And to all of them: the crown of faith."

7. I said: "Lord — may I say just two things? So you can understand what I mean?"

8. He said: "Say what you wish, my Lord."

9. "A great light has appeared before us today," I said. "More beautiful than anything I have seen. Lord — if it is possible — let us build three tabernacles here. One for you. One for Moses. One for Elijah."

10. He smiled at me. "Peter," he said, "you are looking at the kingdom of heaven before it has come."

---
*PNEUMA note: Peter's request for three tabernacles (v.9) is one of the most human moments in the entire APE — the visionary doesn't want to leave. He wants to build a house and stay. The Lord's gentle answer ("You see the kingdom of heaven in advance") is tender, not a rebuke. PNEUMA adds "He smiled at me" — not in source but emotionally consistent with the intimacy of the exchange.*
